chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'hhaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who employs another man for a known wage, and sends him to a property. Then another man gives him dirhams and says, 'Buy such and such with this, and whatever profit you make is between me and you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the one who employed him permits it, there is no problem.'

key_terms.فَلَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on an employee making a profit for a third party while employed by someone else?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* under the chapter on employment wages, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of an employee acting as a sub-agent for a third party, provided the primary employer grants explicit permission. It highlights the Shia legal principle that the employer’s consent validates the employee's authority to manage external funds and share profits, distinguishing this arrangement from unauthorized agency. This ruling underscores the flexibility in commercial contracts within Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing mutual agreement and transparency in profit-sharing agreements.
